q: A note states that the Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction extends to all legal rights while a High Court's is confined to fundamental rights. What is the error?
options: The two jurisdictions have been reversed in the statement
The statement understates both jurisdictions equally
The statement is accurate as to the Supreme Court but not the High Court
The statement is accurate as to the High Court but not the Supreme Court
expl: The wider jurisdiction belongs to the High Court and the narrower to the Supreme Court.
why: Straight reversal is the commonest error in this pairing and is easy to miss because both halves sound orthodox.
trapnote: Check the direction of a comparison. Reversal preserves the vocabulary and inverts the meaning.

q: A note correctly states the tenure of the Comptroller and Auditor General and adds that a minister may remove him. Which statement is correct?
options: Both limbs are right: tenure is six years and removal is at ministerial discretion
The tenure is wrong and the removal is right: the term is five years
Both limbs are wrong: the term is five years and removal is by the President at pleasure
The tenure is right and the removal is wrong: removal mirrors that of a Supreme Court judge
expl: A true first limb is paired with a false second limb.
why: Half-truth construction: the accurate limb lends credibility to the inaccurate one.
trapnote: A correct first half is often there to carry an incorrect second half past you.

q: Consider the criminal statutes in force from July 2024 in relation to writ remedies: 1-Habeas corpus continues to be available. 2-The statutes abolished the writ for custody matters. 3-Remand orders remain examinable. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Constitutional remedies cannot be abolished by an ordinary statute.
why: The second statement is structurally impossible, which is the point the set tests.
trapnote: An ordinary statute cannot abolish a constitutional remedy. The proposition fails on structure alone.

q: The November 2022 ruling is cited as having altered the rules on custody and remand. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: the ruling shortened the permissible period of remand
The citation fails: that ruling concerned reservation and the ceiling doctrine
The citation fails: the ruling concerned the appointment of judges instead
The citation succeeds where the accused belongs to a reserved category
expl: The ruling concerned the economic reservation and had no bearing on custody.
why: The third option misdescribes the subject in a different direction, testing precision rather than recall.
trapnote: Establish the subject-matter of a cited ruling before assessing what it can support.

q: The 2024 nine-judge ruling is cited in a dispute about audit of a public undertaking. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation is misplaced: audit scrutiny is a separate constitutional mechanism
The citation is apt: the ruling defined the scope of audit over public resources
The citation is misplaced: the ruling abolished audit of public undertakings
The citation is apt where the undertaking holds privately owned assets
expl: The ruling concerned a Directive Principle; audit rests on entirely separate provisions.
why: The fourth option builds a bridge between the two subjects that does not exist in either.
trapnote: Two mechanisms can share a subject-matter without being connected in law.

q: It is claimed that the 2023 reservation amendment is already operative and requires one-third of judicial posts to be reserved. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim fails once: the amendment concerns judicial posts but is not yet operative
The claim succeeds: the amendment operated from the date of assent
The claim fails once: the amendment is operative but concerns legislative seats
The claim fails twice: the amendment concerns legislative seats and is not yet operative
expl: The amendment concerns seats in legislatures and awaits a census and delimitation.
why: Two options identify one defect only, so partial knowledge produces a near miss.
trapnote: Two independent defects. The complete option names both.

q: Following the creation of twenty-six districts in Andhra Pradesh, which statement about judicial and audit arrangements is correct?
options: Each new district requires a separate bench of the High Court to be constituted
Each new district requires a separate audit authority to be appointed
More district units fall within the same High Court and the same audit framework
The High Court's territorial jurisdiction is redrawn by the reorganisation itself
expl: Reorganisation multiplies units without altering the constitutional architecture above them.
why: The second and third options assume that administrative multiplication requires institutional multiplication.
trapnote: Administrative units multiply; constitutional institutions above them do not follow automatically.

q: Consider the collegium today: 1-It consists of the Chief Justice and four senior-most judges for Supreme Court appointments. 2-It was displaced by a commission in 2015. 3-It rests on judicial interpretation of the word consultation. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The commission never became operational; the collegium continues.
why: The second statement describes an attempt rather than an accomplished change, which is the distinction tested.
trapnote: An attempted replacement that was struck down did not displace anything.

q: A claim is made that the advisory opinion of November 2025 binds all High Courts as a precedent. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim fails: an advisory opinion is not binding, though it carries great weight
The claim succeeds: all opinions of the Supreme Court bind subordinate courts
The claim fails: the opinion binds the President but not the courts
The claim succeeds where the opinion is delivered by a Constitution Bench
expl: An advisory opinion is advisory; it does not operate as a binding declaration of law.
why: The fourth option ties bindingness to bench strength, which governs precedent for judgments and not opinions.
trapnote: Bench strength governs the weight of judgments. An advisory opinion is not a judgment.

q: A teacher sends a postcard about a bonded child to the Court. Which statement is correct?
options: It must be rejected, only an aggrieved person being entitled to move the Court
It may be treated as a petition only if the child's guardian endorses it
It may be treated as a petition only in a High Court and not the Supreme Court
It may be treated as a petition, the child being unable to approach the Court
expl: Standing is relaxed and a letter may be treated as a petition where the person cannot come themselves.
why: The third and fourth options add conditions that would defeat the very purpose of the relaxation.
trapnote: Any condition that the person concerned must act defeats a relaxation designed for those who cannot.
